ground_truth: Video A uses parsley, sliced round onions, and diced tomatoes as primary vegetables, while video B incorporates cucumber, grated carrots, and green onions. Video A focuses on cutting parsley leaves and onion disks, whereas video B peels cucumber skin and grates carrots. Lemon is used in both, but video B adds lemon zest alongside juice, unlike video A which only uses juice.

In Video B, the chef mixes soy sauce, spicy sauce, and sugar in a bowl before cooking, creating a pre-combined seasoning base. Video A skips this step entirely—the chef adds soy sauce directly to the pan during cooking and never uses sugar. While Video B's sauce is prepared upfront with multiple ingredients, Video A builds the sauce incrementally in the pan.

In video A, the chef uses a mix of ground white pepper, cayenne pepper, and black pepper in the flour coating. In video B, the chef seasons the flour exclusively with black pepper and Sicilian sea salt, omitting white and cayenne peppers entirely. Video A focuses on layered heat from multiple peppers, while video B emphasizes salt-enhanced simplicity.

Video A uses a two-step breading process: first coating chicken in flour before dipping in egg and quinoa mixture. Video B skips the flour stage entirely, directly dipping chicken in egg then panko breadcrumbs. The flour in Video A creates a base layer that helps the quinoa adhere, while Video B achieves crispiness through seasoned panko applied directly to the egg-washed chicken.

In video A, the chef mixes mayonnaise and water with the eggs before cooking, creating an emulsion. In video B, the chef uses only plain cracked eggs without any additional ingredients. Video A's mixture includes dairy fat from mayo and hydration from water, while video B maintains a pure egg base.

In video A, the chef prepares a detailed marinade with olive oil, red wine vinegar, lime juice, and multiple spices to coat the chicken before grilling. Video B shows no marinade preparation - the meat is simply cut and skewered with vegetables without any pre-seasoning or liquid mixture applied.

Video A uses fresh prawns added during the final 2-minute simmer, while Video B incorporates ground chicken sautéed early in the cooking process. The prawns in Video A remain whole and cook briefly to preserve tenderness, whereas Video B breaks up the chicken into small pieces during extended cooking to integrate with other ingredients.

Video A uses a food processor to blend tomatoes with herbs and spices into a uniform mixture, while Video B manually dices tomatoes and cucumbers then mixes them whole with other ingredients. Video B also adds boiled chickpeas and leeks not present in Video A's recipe.

Video A adds caraway spice and Celtic salt directly to the cabbage mixture before mixing by hand, while Video B incorporates sugar, regular salt, and vinegar poured over the cabbage in the jar. Video A mixes ingredients thoroughly before jar packing, whereas Video B adds seasonings in layers during jar filling without hand mixing.

In video A, chefs use plain beaten eggs for coating without additional ingredients, focusing purely on binding the breading. Video B's chefs create an egg mixture by combining eggs with milk, salt, and pepper, adding both flavor and liquid volume to help the breading adhere better while seasoning the meat simultaneously.
